minutes.headline: Lake Shirley's whole-lake herbicide treatment killed invasive fanwort but also cut native plants and clarity
minutes.summary: The Conservation Commission accepted the resignation of Commissioner Chris St. Germaine (appointed an associate member pending town manager approval) and heard several wetlands hearings, approving a septic repair, a garage, and a patio project while continuing three others. The board also heard the annual Lake Shirley report showing last year's whole-lake fluoridone herbicide treatment successfully suppressed invasive fanwort but caused a larger-than-expected drop in native plants and water clarity, approved small payments for a MACC conference and a beaver-deceiver invoice, and discussed a proposed stormwater utility fee, an outdated conservation fee schedule, and Earth Day planning.

what_happened.line: Last year's whole-lake herbicide treatment at Lake Shirley suppressed invasive fanwort but caused a bigger-than-expected drop in native plants and water clarity, the annual report found.
The commission accepted Commissioner Chris St. Germaine's resignation and then voted to add him back as an associate member, pending town manager approval.
The board approved a septic repair, a detached garage, and a patio reconstruction, while continuing hearings on a flood-plain fill project, a culvert replacement, and a house rebuild.
The agent proposed moving the town's outdated conservation fee schedule out of the town charter and into the conservation bylaw so the commission could set fees itself, without a town meeting vote.
A committee update described a proposed residential stormwater utility fee, with commercial properties charged based on their impervious surface area.

why_it_matters: The Lake Shirley plant and clarity data will inform whether the town pursues another herbicide treatment, which affects lake recreation and future treatment costs.
Shifting the fee schedule into the bylaw would let the commission raise conservation permit fees on its own rather than bringing changes to town meeting for a vote.
A stormwater utility fee, if it advances, would show up as a new charge on residential and commercial property owners tied to impervious surface area.
